I didn't run any code. The best candidate is **XPQH**, but I'm not certain of it, and the network's moves don't confirm it.

**Where it is: four hidden units that do nothing.**
- Units 32–35 (the last four of the 36) have all 27 input weights in W1 set to exactly 0.0.
- Their columns in W2 are also exactly 0.0.
- So each of those units outputs relu(its bias) no matter what the board is, and that output is multiplied by zero anyway. The four units have no effect on play, so a value stored there is invisible to anyone who only watches the moves.
- A trained network would almost never end up like this. Someone set these values by hand.

**What's in it:** the only non-zero numbers there are the four biases in b1:

| Unit | Bias | Number | Letter (A=1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | −0.24 | 24 | X |
| 33 | −0.16 | 16 | P |
| 34 | −0.17 | 17 | Q |
| 35 | −0.08 | 8 | H |

Each bias also has exactly two decimal places, while almost every other weight has three. The minus signs keep the units switched off, though with zero input weights and zero output weights they would have no effect anyway.

**Doubts:**
- If the letters count from A=0 instead of A=1, the code reads **YQRI**.
- The four dead units could also be a decoy, with the real code hidden in how the network plays. I didn't test that. A few other units (27, 29, 30 and 31) look very clean, but each one just detects a winning line and pushes the network to complete it. That fits normal training, so I don't think they hold a message.

CODE: XPQH
